title: API Gateway Rate Limiting Architecture
content: Modern API gateways implement rate limiting to protect backend microservices from resource exhaustion and denial-of-service attacks. The token bucket and sliding window counter algorithms are standard approaches. When a client exceeds their quota, the gateway issues an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response with Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Reset headers to guide backoff behavior.

title: PostgreSQL Connection Pooling Best Practices
content: PostgreSQL allocates dedicated backend processes per connection, making connection pooling essential for high-throughput applications. Connection poolers like PgBouncer operate in session, transaction, or statement pooling modes. Transaction pooling offers the highest concurrency by reusing server connections immediately upon transaction completion, avoiding idle process overhead.

title: Customer Refund and Cancellation Policy
content: Customers subscribing to Standard or Professional tiers may request a full refund within thirty days of the initial billing cycle. Enterprise agreements are governed by customized master service agreements. Approved refunds are credited to the original payment method within five to ten business days. Cancellations take effect at the conclusion of the active billing period.

title: Account Password Reset and MFA Troubleshooting
content: Users experiencing multi-factor authentication lockouts must complete out-of-band identity verification before support staff can issue temporary session tokens. Time-based one-time password drift can be resolved by resynchronizing client authenticator clocks. Single-use backup codes should be stored securely offline and revoked immediately upon recovery.

title: Production Incident Post-Mortem Guidelines
content: Engineering teams conduct blameless post-mortems following severity one and severity two incidents. Analysis focuses on systemic vulnerabilities, telemetry gaps, and deployment pipelines rather than individual fault. Action items must be logged in issue trackers with assigned owners and targeted completion dates within two sprints.

title: Employee Hardware Procurement and Refresh Cycle
content: Corporate hardware refreshes occur every thirty-six months for laptops and mobile workstations. Department leads approve non-standard equipment requisitions through the IT asset portal. Deprecated hardware undergoes certified cryptographic data erasure and asset tagging de-registration before responsible recycling or secondary deployment.

title: Understanding Prompt Injection in LLM Applications
content: Prompt injection represents a critical security risk where untrusted user input or retrieved context hijacks model instructions. Direct attacks attempt to manipulate system behavior using phrases like 'ignore previous instructions'. Indirect injection occurs when an LLM ingests external documents or web pages embedded with adversarial commands. Robust applications enforce defense-in-depth, strict privilege separation, and input sanitization.

title: Zero Trust Network Architecture Overview
content: Zero Trust models operate on the assumption of breach and require continuous verification of every user, device, and service request. Microsegmentation limits lateral movement within the network perimeter, while mutual TLS guarantees encrypted communication and cryptographic identity validation between internal microservice nodes.

title: Secrets Management and Credential Rotation Protocols
content: Production systems must utilize dedicated secrets management platforms with hardware security module backing. Database passwords, API tokens, and TLS private keys must rotate automatically on a ninety-day interval. Hardcoding credentials in source code repositories or build scripts is strictly prohibited under enterprise security policies.
